correctness.rationale: Let R=product of r finite commutative local nonfields, s_i=|m_i|>=2, q_i=|R_i/m_i|>=2, S=prod s_i. A unit-coordinate pattern A has w_A=S prod_(i in A)(q_i-1) elements and is adjacent to class B iff A union B=[r]. All non-full classes are independent false twins; the full-unit class is a clique true-twin class, so no forcing set leaves >=2 whites in one class. If <=1 white per class, choose an inclusion-maximal white pattern T; a blue vertex of complementary type T^c exists because w_(T^c)>=2 and sees only the white type T, and iteration clears every white. Hence polynomial u^(N-2^r) prod_A(u+w_A), Z=N-2^r. The Boolean cover matrix becomes tensor powers of the invertible 2x2 disjointness matrix under complement permutation, so has rank 2^r; with M<=Z gives mr=2^r. The multiset of negative root magnitudes has min S and 2^r entries; dividing by S reconstructs all subset products of a_i=q_i-1. Multiplicity of root 1 detects factors a_i=1, and greedily stripping the smallest remaining factor recovers the rest with multiplicity, proving inverse recognition. Independent exhaustive graph-level forcing checks for q,s=(2),(2); (3),(3); (2,2),(2,2) reproduced the full polynomial; generality follows from the inclusion-maximal and subset-product proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete natural graph-set enumerator and recovers r, product of maximal-ideal cardinalities and all residue-field orders from a graph polynomial. Such inverse reconstruction describes exactly what a standard combinatorial invariant remembers about a semilocal ring; the inability to recover each s_i separately is an explicit sharp limitation. The H-join structure alone does not make the forcing or inverse result a routine textbook identity.
